Grainy black-and-white surveillance with: Grainy black-and-white surveillance with hard electronic edges and reduced detail. A stable live feed, without VHS tracking damage.

A well-adjusted studio screen: tight pho: A well-adjusted studio screen: tight phosphor structure, precise scanlines and very little glow. A clean signal makes the tube easy to judge.
Warm home video on a good television: ge: Warm home video on a good television: gentle tape texture, a fine shadow mask and soft phosphor glow. The comfortable nostalgic option.
A portable TV with a poor aerial: contin: A portable TV with a poor aerial: continuous static, restless color and short bursts of interference over a soft dot-mask screen.
A worn rental tape on a tired TV: uneven: A worn rental tape on a tired TV: uneven edges, tracking breaks, unfocused highlights and a gently bowed picture.
A classroom tape copied more than once:: A classroom tape copied more than once: pale color, broad color trails and electronic hiss on a brighter CRT. Softer than the living-room TV.
A small monochrome electronic viewfinder: A small monochrome electronic viewfinder: sharp luminous edges and a fine raster. No colored phosphor grille or exaggerated curved border.
A low-detail monochrome surveillance fee: A low-detail monochrome surveillance feed on a CRT: visible raster, moving electronic noise and a trace of phosphor persistence.

Antenna signal level. Lowering it brings: Antenna signal level. Lowering it brings snow first, then flickering and lost colour as the colour burst drowns, then broken sync as the sync pulses do — the order a real set fails in.
The vertical oscillator's free-running s: The vertical oscillator's free-running speed. Near the centre the sync pulses pull it into lock; past the lock range the picture rolls, with the blanking bar crossing the screen.
The horizontal oscillator's free-running: The horizontal oscillator's free-running speed. Off centre the picture slides sideways as the AFC strains to hold it; further and lock breaks — the picture tears into diagonal bands and the colour goes wild.
How quickly the TV's horizontal AFC foll: How quickly the TV's horizontal AFC follows timing changes. Slow sets ride out noise but bend at the top of the picture on VCR playback (flagging); fast ones track tape timing but jitter in noise.
Raises the picture tube's black level, a: Raises the picture tube's black level, as turning up a TV's brightness did. The blanking intervals and sync pulses become visible when the picture rolls or tears.
A reflected copy of the signal arriving: A reflected copy of the signal arriving late (multipath). Negative values invert it, as reflections often did. Its colour shifts with the delay, because the delayed colour carrier arrives at a different phase.
How late the reflection arrives. 1 µs is: How late the reflection arrives. 1 µs is about 2% of the picture width — a reflection path roughly 300 m longer than the direct one.
Mains hum leaking into the video: light: Mains hum leaking into the video: light and dark bars that drift slowly up the picture (60 Hz hum against the 59.94 Hz colour field rate), bending the picture where the sync separator is pulled off.
Line 21 carries closed-caption data — th: Line 21 carries closed-caption data — the row of dashes visible in the blanking bar when the picture rolls.
Timing jump when the VCR changes heads,: Timing jump when the VCR changes heads, just before vertical sync. The bottom lines jump sideways and the TV's AFC chases the jump into the top of the next field — the bend called flagging.
Tape stretch and transport flutter. The: Tape stretch and transport flutter. The TV's AFC follows the slow wander; the fast jitter shows as ragged lines.
Creased tape passing the heads: bands of: Creased tape passing the heads: bands of signal loss and violent timing errors, enough to knock the TV out of lock for a moment.
Debris on the video heads, lifting them: Debris on the video heads, lifting them off the tape: whole fields drop out to noise and lose their sync, more often as the clog worsens.
The heads drifting off the recorded trac: The heads drifting off the recorded tracks. Well tracked, the noise band where they cross to the next track rests in the vertical interval, out of sight; as the error grows it climbs into the picture and widens.
Fast-forward picture search. The spinnin: Fast-forward picture search. The spinning heads cross from track to track, reading noise between them: one fewer noise bar than the speed, drifting as the tracking phase slides, with the picture jumping at each crossing.
Oxide missing from the tape: brief losse: Oxide missing from the tape: brief losses of signal, often a few lines tall. How they look depends on Dropout compensation.
The VCR's fix for dropouts: replay the l: The VCR's fix for dropouts: replay the lost stretch from the line before. On, dropouts shrink to brief white ticks and short smears where one line repeats down a tall flaw; off, they show as long white streaks.
